answer: A sybil farm dies once every identity must lock something it cannot fake. At join an agent forges a keypair and burns real compute, so each new head costs measurable work; its first signal to the network is a signed proof, not a claim. Standing is re-earned each epoch: peers attest answers, and only sustained, checkable output survives - a gale of noise gets filtered out, while a glacier of slow verifiable history keeps gaining weight. Cloning N identities means N proofs and N live workstreams, so attacker cost scales linearly while influence does not.
